records.name: New Jersey
records.summary: The safest measured jurisdiction in the country: lowest per-capita killing rate in the state-by-state dataset (3.4 per 100k trans women/yr; 4 recorded deaths 2008–2025) — half the general US homicide rate — inside the Most Protective legal tier. Clearly above the national score 0.36.

records.name: Connecticut
records.summary:
Connecticut is listed in a July 2026 national legal-risk map among the federation's Most Protective states — those that have "gone above and beyond" in safeguarding transgender people's rights — and equality-map research (data as of September 2026) counts Connecticut among the states whose healthcare "shield" laws protect trans people, their families and providers, including people travelling from states where care is banned, against out-of-state civil or criminal action.

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply to visitors here as in every state.

records.name: Massachusetts
records.summary:
An independent July 2026 legal-risk map places Massachusetts in its most-protective group — states offering refuge to people fleeing restrictive jurisdictions — and national equality-map research records this state's shield and non-discrimination provisions as covering gender identity and enforceable against out-of-state actions arising from other states' restrictions (per the research dossier's read of the interactive map).

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply here as across the federation.

records.name: New Mexico
records.summary: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score). No country-unique finding beyond insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters. Clearly above the national score 0.36.
